extra.message: Remote Code Execution via Insecure Pickle Deserialization in Dockerized Lab — Full remote code execution on the lab container, potentially enabling container breakout or access to host resources. [verified: The /deserialize endpoint in dockerized_labs/insec_des_lab/main.py:28-31 reads attacker-controlled form field serialized_data, base64-decodes it, and passes the result directly to pickle.loads() with no authentication, integrity check, or restricted unpickler — textbook RCE via insecure deserialization.]

Unauthenticated Exposure of All Users' PII and Secrets via API — Any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve all users' credit card numbers, SSNs, and API keys in plaintext via a single API call. [verified: The `all_users_data_view` at `/api/all-users/` has zero authentication: no `@login_required`, no `request.user.is_authenticated` check, and the code comments explicitly state 'ANY user (even unauthenticated ones!)' can access it. The Docker lab's settings offer no compensating global auth guard.]

Unauthenticated Mass Exposure of All Users' Sensitive PII — Catastrophic data breach: complete exposure of all users' credit cards, SSNs, and API keys to any unauthenticated attacker. [verified: Same endpoint as finding [0] — `all_users_data_view` returns all users' credit cards, SSNs, and API keys in JSON with no authentication check whatsoever, confirmed by the function body at lines 112-132 and the explicit comment acknowledging the missing control.]

Security Misconfiguration — DEBUG=True, ALLOWED_HOSTS=['*'], Hardcoded Secret — Information disclosure via debug pages, host header injection attacks, and session forgery via hardcoded secret key. [verified: settings.py lines 11–14 confirm DEBUG=True, ALLOWED_HOSTS=['*'], and SECRET_KEY='django-insecure-key-for-demonstration-only'; Dockerfile exposes port 8000 to host, making debug stack traces, host-header injection, and session forgery via known key trivially reachable from any network attacker targeting the container.]

Arbitrary Code Execution via User-Written Python Module Files — Remote code execution — attacker can write and execute arbitrary Python on the server [verified: log_function_checker writes attacker-controlled code to playground/A9/main.py and api.py (imported at top-level in apis.py:10 and urls.py:3); Python's module cache prevents immediate intra-process re-import, but with DEBUG=True the Django auto-reloader detects the disk change, restarts, and executes the injected code on reload.]

Missing authentication on log_function_checker — unauthenticated arbitrary Python file write leading to code execution — An unauthenticated attacker can overwrite server-side Python source files with arbitrary code, achieving remote code execution on the application server when the auto-reloader triggers or the server restarts. [verified: MISSING-CONTROL: @authentication_decorator is explicitly commented out on log_function_checker (apis.py:60-61) with no other auth check in the function body; @csrf_exempt is active. No compensating control exists — any unauthenticated attacker can POST to /2021/discussion/A9/api and overwrite server Python modules.]

Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Write of Executable Python Code — Attacker can write arbitrary Python code to the application's source tree without authentication, achieving code execution on server restart or via other code paths that reload modules. [verified: Identical to finding 0 — log_function_checker at apis.py:59-89 writes unauthenticated attacker-supplied log_code/api_code to importable A9 module files with no validation or auth. @authentication_decorator is commented out, @csrf_exempt is present, and DEBUG=True enables auto-reloader execution of the injected code.]

Unauthenticated arbitrary file write to server Python modules in log_function_checker — Unauthenticated attacker can write arbitrary Python code to server‑side importable modules, achieving remote code execution on the next server restart or import cycle. [verified: The @authentication_decorator is commented out (apis.py:60), @csrf_exempt is active, and user-supplied log_code/api_code POST params are written via open(...,'w').write() to importable Python module files playground/A9/main.py and api.py (lines 68-71). With DEBUG=True (settings.py:34), Django's auto-reloader detects the file change, restarts, and loads the attacker's injected code from the top-lev]

Arbitrary Code Execution via Code Playground File Overwrite — Remote code execution — attacker-controlled Python code executed on the server [verified: A6_disscussion_api_2 writes attacker-controlled code to playground/A6/utility.py (imported at apis.py:9). The immediate check_vuln() call in A6_disscussion_api uses the cached module, but the file persists on disk and DEBUG=True causes auto-reloader restart, loading the injected code on next server start.]

Missing authentication on A6_disscussion_api_2 — unauthenticated arbitrary Python file write leading to code execution — An unauthenticated attacker can overwrite server-side Python source files with arbitrary code, achieving remote code execution when the auto-reloader triggers or the server restarts. [verified: MISSING-CONTROL: A6_disscussion_api_2 (apis.py:126-137) has no authentication decorator, no request.user check, and only @csrf_exempt. No auth control exists whatsoever on this endpoint at /2021/discussion/A6/api2 — any unauthenticated attacker can overwrite the importable utility.py module.]

Unauthenticated arbitrary file write to server Python modules in A6_disscussion_api_2 — Unauthenticated attacker can write arbitrary Python code to server‑side importable modules, achieving remote code execution on the next server restart or import cycle. [verified: A6_disscussion_api_2 has no authentication decorator, only @csrf_exempt (apis.py:125), and writes user-supplied POST['code'] directly to playground/A6/utility.py (line 133), which is imported at module level at apis.py:9. With DEBUG=True, the auto-reloader restarts and executes the injected code; no validation, sanitization, or auth check exists.]

Code Injection via eval() in mitre_lab_25_api — Attacker executes arbitrary Python code server-side. [verified: User-controlled POST parameter 'expression' flows directly into eval() at line 218 with no validation, sanitization, or authentication (the @authentication_decorator is commented out at line 214).]

Code Injection via eval() in mitre_lab_25_api — Full arbitrary Python code execution on the server, complete system compromise [verified: eval(expression) at line 218 receives attacker-controlled POST data with zero sanitization; the @authentication_decorator is commented out at line 214 and @csrf_exempt is present, enabling unauthenticated arbitrary Python execution.]

OS Command Injection via nmap Command Concatenation — Attacker executes arbitrary OS commands via nmap command injection. [verified: User-supplied POST 'ip' is concatenated into 'nmap ' + ip at line 239 and executed via subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True) in command_out at line 234 with no sanitization, allowing shell metacharacter injection.]

OS Command Injection via subprocess.Popen with shell=True in mitre_lab_17_api — Remote code execution on the server host — full filesystem access, reverse shell [verified: subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True) at line 234 executes a command built from unsanitized user POST 'ip' at line 239; shell=True with attacker-controlled input yields full OS command injection.]

Code Injection via eval() with missing authentication in mitre_lab_25_api — Unauthenticated remote code execution. Any attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server without credentials. [verified: eval(expression) at line 218 with the authentication decorator commented out (line 214) means any unauthenticated attacker can submit arbitrary Python code for immediate server-side execution.]

SQL Injection via Raw Query String Concatenation in sql_lab — Authentication bypass, full SQLite database dump (all user credentials, secrets, flags), arbitrary data modification or deletion [verified: Duplicate of finding 0: SQL injection via raw query with string concatenation in sql_lab.]

SQL Injection via Raw Query String Concatenation in sql_lab — Attacker bypasses authentication, exfiltrates database contents, or modifies data in the SQLite database. [verified: User-supplied POST params 'name'/'password' concatenated directly into raw SQL query string without parameterization, executed via login.objects.raw(); no input sanitization or ORM escaping present.]

Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads() on Attacker-Controlled Cookie — Remote code execution via crafted pickle payload — full server compromise [verified: Duplicate of finding 6: pickle.loads on attacker-controlled base64-decoded cookie enables RCE.]

SQL Injection via Raw Query String Concatenation in sql_lab — Attacker can bypass authentication, extract all rows from the login table, or perform arbitrary SQL operations on the SQLite database. [verified: Duplicate of finding 0: same raw SQL concatenation of user POST params into query string executed via login.objects.raw() with no parameterization.]

Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads on Attacker-Controlled Cookie — Remote code execution on the server by crafting a malicious pickled object and setting it as the token cookie. [verified: Duplicate of finding 6: base64-decoded cookie passed to pickle.loads() enabling arbitrary code execution via crafted pickled objects.]

Insecure Deserialization via pickle.loads on Attacker-Controlled Cookie — Attacker achieves remote code execution by sending a malicious serialized Python object in the token cookie. [verified: User-controlled 'token' cookie is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads() with no integrity check; attacker can craft malicious pickled objects for arbitrary code execution on deserialization.]

OS Command Injection via subprocess.Popen with shell=True in cmd_lab — Remote code execution on the server host — full filesystem access, reverse shell, lateral movement to Docker host [verified: Duplicate of finding 2: command injection via subprocess.Popen shell=True with user-controlled domain.]

Code Injection via eval() on User Input in cmd_lab2 — Full arbitrary Python code execution on the server, complete system compromise [verified: Duplicate of finding 3: code injection via unsandboxed eval() on user input.]

Insecure YAML Deserialization Allowing Arbitrary Code Execution — Remote code execution via malicious YAML payload — full server compromise [verified: Duplicate of finding 7: yaml.load with unsafe Loader on user-uploaded YAML enables RCE.]

Code Injection via Pillow ImageMath.eval on User-Controlled Expression — Remote code execution via crafted Pillow ImageMath expression [verified: Duplicate of finding 4: Pillow ImageMath.eval on user-controlled function_str with vulnerable Pillow 9.4.0.]

Command Injection via shell=True with User-Controlled Domain — Remote code execution on the server OS. Attacker can run arbitrary shell commands with the web server's privileges. [verified: Duplicate of finding 2: user domain POST param interpolated into dig/nslookup command executed via subprocess.Popen with shell=True; shell metacharacters unfiltered.]

Remote Code Execution via eval() on User Input — Unrestricted Python code execution with the web server's privileges, enabling complete system takeover. [verified: Duplicate of finding 3: direct eval() on user-supplied POST param with no restrictions.]

SQL Injection via Raw Query in injection_sql_lab — Authentication bypass, data exfiltration from sql_lab_table, SQLite database compromise [verified: Duplicate of finding 1: SQL injection via raw query in injection_sql_lab.]

Insecure YAML Deserialization via yaml.load with unsafe Loader in a9_lab — Remote code execution on the server via crafted YAML payload containing Python object instantiation directives. [verified: Duplicate of finding 7: yaml.load(file, yaml.Loader) with PyYAML 5.1 enables arbitrary Python object deserialization.]

Code Injection via Pillow ImageMath.eval on User-Controlled Expression — Remote code execution on the server through crafted ImageMath expression payloads. [verified: Duplicate of finding 4: user function_str passed to Pillow ImageMath.eval() enabling arbitrary Python code execution.]

SQL Injection via Raw Query in injection_sql_lab — Attacker can bypass authentication and extract all rows from the sql_lab_table. [verified: Duplicate of finding 1: same raw SQL concatenation in injection_sql_lab executed via sql_lab_table.objects.raw() with no parameterization.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY in Source Code — Session forgery, CSRF token bypass, and password reset token manipulation, leading to full application compromise. [verified: SECRET_KEY='lr66%-a!$km5ed@n5ug!tya5bv!0(yqwa1tn!q%0%3m2nh%oml' is hardcoded in plaintext on settings.py:23 and committed to source control; used by Django for cryptographic signing of sessions, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens across the entire application with no compensating control.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY and DEBUG=True in Production Configuration — Attacker can forge signed cookies/sessions, predict CSRF tokens, and access detailed error stack traces revealing source code paths and configuration values. [verified: SECRET_KEY='lr66%-a!$km5ed@n5ug!tya5bv!0(yqwa1tn!q%0%3m2nh%oml' is hardcoded on settings.py:23 AND DEBUG=True on line 30; together the key is exposed via error pages and enables session forgery, CSRF token prediction, and full application compromise.]

Hardcoded JWT Signing Secret in Source Code — Attacker forges valid JWT tokens to impersonate any user in the CSRF lab functionality. [verified: The literal string 'csrf_vulneribility' is hardcoded as the JWT signing secret at line 158 and used for verification at line 183; an attacker with source access can forge valid tokens to impersonate any user in the CSRF lab.]

CSRF on State-Changing GET Endpoint for Money Transfer — Cross-site request forgery — attacker can force authenticated victim to transfer money to attacker's account [verified: csrf_transfer_monei_api at line 191 is a GET-mapped endpoint that transfers money between accounts; Django CSRF middleware never checks GET, and no per-view CSRF token or @authentication_decorator is enforced.]

CSRF on State-Changing Money Transfer via GET Request — Attacker can force authenticated users to transfer money to an attacker-controlled account by tricking them into visiting a malicious page. [verified: The GET-based csrf_transfer_monei_api at line 191 modifies account balances without any CSRF token verification; Django middleware exempts GET, and the JWT cookie has no Secure/HttpOnly flags set explicitly.]

Hardcoded weak JWT signing secret in csrf_lab_login — Attackers can forge JWT tokens to impersonate any user and bypass authentication in the CSRF lab and money transfer endpoints. [verified: 'csrf_vulneribility' is a plaintext hardcoded JWT secret at line 158 and line 183; anyone with knowledge of this secret can sign forged auth_cookiee tokens to impersonate arbitrary users in the CSRF lab.]

Plaintext password storage in login and authLogin models — If the database is compromised (e.g., via SQL injection), all user passwords are exposed in plaintext, enabling credential stuffing and account takeover across services. [verified: authLogin model stores passwords in plaintext CharField(200) with no hashing; views.py:287 directly writes raw POST password via authLogin.objects.create, and views.py:315 compares plaintext on login — both reachable via /auth_lab/signup and /auth_lab/login. The login model portion is dead code (no view writes to it), but authLogin alone confirms the finding.]

Reflected XSS via Alphanumeric-Stripping Filter Bypass in xss_lab3 — An attacker can craft a POST request with a JSFuck-encoded XSS payload that bypasses the alphanumeric filter and Django autoescaping (which does not affect []()!+ characters), executing arbitrary JavaScript in the context of an authenticated victim's session, enabling session theft, credential harvesting, or arbitrary actions as the victim. [verified: POST-supplied 'username' is filtered only by r'[a-zA-Z0-9]' and rendered as {{code}} inside a <script> tag; Django autoescaping escapes only <>&"' but JSFuck payloads of []()!+ pass through unmodified and execute as JavaScript.]

XML External Entity Injection via External General Entities Enabled — Local file disclosure (/etc/passwd, settings.py with SECRET_KEY), internal SSRF, denial of service via billion laughs attack [verified: Duplicate of finding 8: XXE via SAX parser with feature_external_ges=True parsing attacker-controlled XML.]

Plaintext Password Storage and Comparison — Complete credential compromise if database is accessed; all user passwords exposed in plaintext [verified: authLab model stores passwords in plaintext CharField; comparisons done in plaintext via authLogin.objects.filter(username=...,password=...); database compromise exposes all credentials.]

IDOR via Predictable User ID in Cookie — Account takeover — impersonate any user by guessing/setting their userid cookie [verified: Duplicate of finding 15: userid cookie used to authenticate users without password verification in GET path.]

Broken Access Control via Client-Side Admin Cookie Manipulation — Privilege escalation from regular user to admin, access to admin-only secret data [verified: Duplicate of finding 11: admin=1 cookie check without server-side signature enables privilege escalation.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via SAX Parser with External Entities Enabled — Attacker reads arbitrary files from the server filesystem (e.g., /etc/passwd, settings.py with secrets) and performs SSRF attacks. [verified: SAX parser explicitly enables external general entities (feature_external_ges=True) and parses attacker-controlled XML from request.body; allows local file reads and SSRF via crafted external entity references.]

Weak OTP Generation and Missing Brute-Force Protection — Account takeover via OTP brute-force (max 900 attempts); admin OTP can be triggered repeatedly until guessed [verified: Duplicate of finding 20: OTP generation via randint(100,999) with no rate limiting, brute-forceable in ~900 attempts.]

IDOR / Broken Authentication via cookie-based user identification in auth_lab_login — Complete account takeover of any user by manipulating the userid cookie value. Attacker can impersonate any registered user. [verified: Duplicate of finding 15: cookie-based userid lookup in auth_lab_login GET enables IDOR/impersonation.]

Broken Access Control via X-Host Header Spoofing — Access to admin-only secret key 'S3CR37K3Y' via header manipulation [verified: Duplicate of finding 13: X-Host header used for access control to secret S3CR37K3Y.]

Broken Access Control via Client-Side Cookie admin=1 Check — Any authenticated user can gain admin privileges by setting a browser cookie, bypassing all server-side authorization. [verified: Admin access granted solely by checking client-controlled cookie request.COOKIES.get('admin')=='1' with no server-side signature or validation; any user can set admin=1 to escalate privileges.]

Privilege Escalation via Client-Side Admin Cookie — Complete privilege escalation: any user can become admin by setting a cookie, gaining access to sensitive admin secrets. [verified: Duplicate of finding 11: admin access via client-controlled admin=1 cookie with no server-side validation.]

Broken Access Control via User-Agent Header Manipulation — Privilege escalation to admin via trivial HTTP header manipulation [verified: Duplicate of finding 12: User-Agent header used for admin authorization, trivially spoofed.]

Missing Authorization on Admin Secret Endpoint — Any logged-in user can access admin-only secret information [verified: Duplicate of finding 14: secret endpoint only checks is_authenticated with no role verification.]

Weak OTP — 3-Digit Code Brute-Forceable with No Rate Limiting — Attacker can bypass OTP-based two-factor authentication by brute-forcing the 3-digit code within minutes. [verified: Duplicate of finding 20: 3-digit OTP with 900 values, no rate limiting, brute-forceable in seconds.]

Brute-forceable OTP with only 900 possible values and no rate limiting — An attacker can brute-force the OTP for any email address in seconds, bypassing the two-factor authentication mechanism. [verified: Duplicate of finding 20: 3-digit OTP with only 900 values and no rate limiting enables brute-force in seconds.]

Weak OTP Generation — 3-Digit Non-Cryptographic Random — OTP/2FA bypass via brute-force, allowing unauthorized access to accounts even when OTP verification is enabled. [verified: Duplicate of finding 20: 3-digit non-cryptographic OTP with 900 values and no rate limiting.]

Brute-Forceable OTP — 3-Digit Code with No Rate Limiting — Attacker brute-forces OTP codes to bypass two-factor authentication and impersonate users. [verified: OTP generated as randint(100,999) with only 900 values, no rate limiting on verification endpoint, no expiration, no attempt lockout; brute-forceable within ~900 requests.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via User-Controlled File Path — Read arbitrary files on the server filesystem — SECRET_KEY, database, source code, /etc/passwd [verified: Duplicate of finding 10: path traversal via user-controlled file path joined with os.path.join and opened without validation.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via Unvalidated requests.get() on User URL — Internal network reconnaissance, access to internal services and metadata endpoints, potential file:// reads [verified: Duplicate of finding 9: SSRF via unvalidated requests.get() on user-provided URL.]

Broken Access Control via X-Host Header Spoofing for Secret Access — Attacker spoofs X-Host header to access secret data intended only for admin subdomain. [verified: Access to secret S3CR37K3Y controlled by X-Host header check; attacker can set X-Host:admin.localhost:8000 to bypass the check.]

Server-Side Template Injection via User-Written Template Files — Arbitrary code execution via Django template engine, access to all context variables, settings disclosure including SECRET_KEY [verified: Duplicate of finding 5: SSTI via Django template rendering of user-written blog file; info disclosure not arbitrary RCE.]

Weak Password Hashing Using Unsalted MD5 — Password cracking via rainbow tables and MD5 collision attacks; credential compromise [verified: Duplicate of finding 18: unsalted MD5 password hashing vulnerable to rainbow table attacks.]

Unsigned Client-Side Authentication Cookie Allowing Privilege Escalation — Privilege escalation to admin via cookie forgery — no cryptographic protection [verified: crypto_failure_lab3 auth cookie is f'{username}|{expire}' with no HMAC/signature; attacker can trivially forge admin|2099-... to gain admin privileges.]

Broken Access Control via Client-Side Admin Cookie in a1_broken_access_lab_1 — An attacker can set admin=1 in their browser cookies to gain unauthorized admin access to the endpoint, exposing the secret key '0NLY_F0R_4DM1N5' without any valid credentials or server-side verification. [verified: a1_broken_access_lab_1 authorizes admin access via request.COOKIES.get('admin')=='1'—a purely client-controlled cookie—with no server-side verification, allowing any authenticated user to trivially set admin=1 and read '0NLY_F0R_4DM1N5'.]

Missing Authorization on Secret Admin Endpoint — Any authenticated user can access privileged admin content, bypassing the intended role-based access control. [verified: Duplicate of finding 14: secret endpoint missing role-based authorization, accessible to any authenticated user.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read via user-controlled path in ssrf_lab — Arbitrary file read on the server filesystem, including source code, configuration files (settings.py with SECRET_KEY), database files, and system files. [verified: Duplicate of finding 10: user-supplied file path in os.path.join permits ../ traversal and absolute path bypass.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via user-controlled URL in ssrf_lab2 — Access to internal network services, admin interfaces, cloud metadata endpoints, and potential remote code execution if combined with other vulnerabilities. [verified: Duplicate of finding 9: requests.get(url) on user URL with no allowlisting enables SSRF.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via Unvalidated URL Fetch — Attacker can scan internal networks, access internal services (including cloud metadata), and potentially pivot to other systems. [verified: Duplicate of finding 9: user URL fetched via requests.get() with no validation, enabling SSRF against internal services.]

Server-Side Template Injection via User Content Written to Template File — Remote code execution through SSTI, allowing complete server compromise when the blog post is viewed. [verified: Duplicate of finding 5: SSTI via blog content rendered as Django template; info disclosure via template tags, not Jinja2 RCE.]

Weak cryptographic hashing (MD5 without salt) for password storage in crypto_failure_lab — Stored password hashes can be cracked using rainbow tables or brute-force attacks due to the use of unsalted MD5. [verified: Duplicate of finding 18: unsalted MD5 password hashing is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to rainbow tables.]

Cookie forgery via unsigned/una authenticated cookie in crypto_failure_lab3 — An attacker can forge admin cookies by setting cookie=admin|2099-12-31... to gain unauthorized admin access without credentials. [verified: Duplicate of finding 76: unsigned cookie format f'{username}|{expire}' enables trivial admin cookie forgery.]

Weak JWT Secret — Trivially Guessable Hardcoded Key Enables Token Forgery — Attacker can forge admin-authenticated JWT cookies, gaining unauthorized admin access to the application. [verified: JWT signing secret SECRET_COOKIE_KEY hardcoded as 'PYGOAT' in settings.py; attacker can forge admin JWT tokens using this publicly guessable secret.]

DEBUG=True enabled exposing sensitive debug information — Stack traces reveal source code paths, database queries, settings values including SECRET_KEY, and internal application structure to attackers. [verified: DEBUG=True on settings.py:30 is not overridden in the Dockerfile deploying with gunicorn; reachable error paths expose stack traces with SECRET_KEY, SENSITIVE_DATA, and internal settings to any authenticated user.]

DEBUG=True Enabled in Production Deployment — Information disclosure: verbose error pages expose stack traces, file paths, settings, and potentially sensitive data to attackers. [verified: DEBUG=True on settings.py:30 is not overridden in the Dockerfile which deploys with gunicorn; reachable authenticated endpoints that throw exceptions will leak full stack traces with settings and file paths.]

Weak Hardcoded JWT Signing Key Enabling Admin Impersonation — Complete authentication bypass: forged JWT tokens grant admin access to the security misconfiguration lab. [verified: SECRET_COOKIE_KEY='PYGOAT' on settings.py:171 is used to sign JWT auth_cookie tokens in sec_misconfig_lab3 (introduction/views.py:1095,1107); the key is trivially guessable, allowing any attacker to forge a JWT with user='admin' and gain admin access.]

Hardcoded Weak JWT Secret Key Enabling Token Forgery — JWT token forgery — any attacker can create admin-level auth_cookie JWTs and gain administrator access [verified: SECRET_COOKIE_KEY='PYGOAT' on settings.py:171 signs JWT auth_cookie in sec_misconfig_lab3; the trivially guessable key allows forging admin JWTs to bypass authentication on the lab endpoint.]

Sensitive Credentials Logged in Plaintext — User credentials exposed in application log files accessible to anyone with log access [verified: api.py line 14 passes plaintext username and password to L.info() unconditionally on POST; the active Log.info() in main.py is a no-op stub only because the learner hasn't implemented it yet, but archive.py shows the intended implementation writes credentials verbatim to test.log, confirming the sensitive-data-logging design flaw.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Credential brute-forcing, OTP brute-forcing, account enumeration, denial of service via repeated auth attempts [verified: No Django-ratelimit, throttle decorators, or attempt counting on most auth endpoints (login, register, OTP); auth_failure_lab2 does have lockout but all other endpoints are unprotected against brute-force.]

Reflected XSS via unsafe GET parameter in xss_lab — Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser, steal session cookies, perform actions as the victim, or deface the page. [verified: GET parameter 'q' passed unsanitized to template xss_lab.html which renders it with |safe filter, explicitly bypassing Django auto-escaping; classic reflected XSS.]

Stored/Reflected XSS with bypassable filter in xss_lab2 — Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser by submitting a POST with a filtered but bypassable XSS payload. [verified: POST 'username' filtered only by naive .replace('

Account Enumeration via Distinct Error Messages on Login — Attacker enumerates valid usernames in the system, facilitating targeted password attacks. [verified: sql_lab returns distinct responses for 'User not found' vs wrong password allowing username enumeration by observing response differences.]

User Enumeration via Distinct Error Messages in Login — Attacker can enumerate valid usernames in the system, facilitating targeted password guessing or credential stuffing attacks. [verified: Duplicate of finding 21: distinct error messages for user-not-found vs wrong-password enable username enumeration.]

Insecure Cookie Flags — Missing Secure, SameSite=None on Auth Cookies — Session/token theft via MITM on unencrypted connections; CSRF-based cookie exfiltration [verified: Duplicate of finding 17: insecure cookie flags (secure=False, samesite=None, no HttpOnly).]

Insecure Cookie Configuration — Missing Secure, HttpOnly Flags with SameSite=None — Session cookies can be stolen via XSS (no HttpOnly), intercepted over unencrypted connections (no Secure), and sent in cross-site requests enabling CSRF attacks (SameSite=None). [verified: Duplicate of finding 17: auth cookies set with secure=False, samesite=None, no HttpOnly; vulnerable to MITM and XSS theft.]

Exposed Debug Log Endpoint Leaking Internal Information — Information disclosure — attackers learn server file paths, application structure, error details, and internal operation patterns [verified: Duplicate of finding 16: /debug endpoint serves debug.log without authentication, exposing internal paths.]

User enumeration via distinct error messages in login in a10_lab — An attacker can enumerate valid usernames by observing different error responses, facilitating targeted password attacks. [verified: Duplicate of finding 21: a10_lab returns distinct responses for nonexistent vs wrong-password enabling user enumeration.]

Debug log file exposure via /debug endpoint — Exposure of application debug information, stack traces, and potentially sensitive data logged during application operation. [verified: Duplicate of finding 16: /debug endpoint serves static debug.log template without any authentication check.]

Sensitive Data (Usernames) Written to Application Logs — Usernames and IP addresses are stored in plaintext logs accessible via the /debug endpoint. [verified: Usernames and IP addresses logged via logging.warning/info on successful login; log content exposed via the /debug endpoint.]

IDOR — any authenticated user can view arbitrary blogs via ssti_view_blog — Authenticated users can access blog content belonging to other users, bypassing the per-user scoping enforced in the blog listing view. [verified: ssti_view_blog checks only is_authenticated but not blog ownership (Blogs.author FK); blog_id is uuid segment (~65K values) making enumeration feasible, but the practical risk is limited since IDs must be obtained or brute-forced.]

Reflected XSS via |safe in A8 Software Integrity lab — Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser by crafting a malicious link with script tags in the `username` parameter, leading to session theft, credential phishing, or page defacement. [verified: GET 'username' parameter in software_and_data_integrity_failure_lab2 rendered with |safe filter in lab2.html; reflected XSS in an A8 lab endpoint unrelated to XSS training labs.]

Log Injection via Unsanitized X-Forwarded-For Header — Log forgery, log poisoning, log-viewer compromise, evasion of monitoring and incident response [verified: Duplicate of finding 22: unsanitized X-Forwarded-For in log entries enables log injection.]

Log Injection via User-Controlled X-Forwarded-For Header — Log forgery enabling an attacker to inject fake entries, hide malicious activity, and corrupt log-based monitoring and forensics. [verified: Duplicate of finding 22: X-Forwarded-For header unsanitized in log entries allows log injection.]
